title: Ops signal capture (ad-hoc lightweight sheet)
content:
Purpose:
This is a quick, low-friction collector for one-off operational signals and small cross-team asks that pop up during launches or regression windows. Intended for short-lived tracking (2–6 weeks). Use this instead of spinning up a full ticket board when the work is small and coordination is lightweight.

How to use (notes):
- Owner should update the row at least once per day while active.
- Mark Priority as S1/S2/S3 (S1 = user impacting, S3 = informational).
- If an item grows beyond ~8h or touches 3+ teams, create a Jira and move the ticket link to the "Action" cell.
- This sheet lives in company/misc as a temporary artifact; copy to product-specific folder if it becomes persistent.

Columns (header row):
ID | Signal source | Short description | Priority | Current owner | Last seen (YYYY-MM-DD) | Action / next step | Dependents | Est hrs (rough) | Notes / links

Sample rows:
1 | api-throttle-alert | High 95th latency on gpt-medium under prod burst tests | S1 | Marco Alvarez | 2029-02-12 | Run targeted traffic test against dedicated cluster; compare kernel profile | serving-runtime, infra | 6 | e2e test id: test-2029-02-12-03; possibly batching config regression
2 | cost-spike-notice | Unexpected spike in embedding unit cost for search-qa | S2 | Leah O'Connor | 2029-02-11 | Check cache-hit ratios & eviction logs; validate quantization variant used | optimize, observability | 4 | linked logs: s3://ops-logs/emb-cost/feb11
3 | canary-fallback | Canary for v2 model falling back to v1 with increased latency | S1 | Jamal Singh | 2029-02-12 | Roll canary back for traffic > 10 rps; open rollback PR if needed | product-hosted-api, release-engineering | 3 | PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release/pull/1199
4 | region-degen | Europe region serving errors (502) intermittently across routes | S1 | Priya Kapoor | 2029-02-09 | Swap traffic to alt-region, monitor error-rate for 2h | infra, sre | 5 | incident stub: INF-2381; customer impact flagged
5 | metrics-drift | Tokenization mismatch causing embeddings drift vs. baseline | S2 | Marco Alvarez | 2029-02-10 | Re-run consistency job; validate tokenizer library version | applied-ml | 2 | baseline run id: run-2029-02-08
6 | small-ask | Sales requested short latency audit for demo next week | S3 | Leah O'Connor | 2029-02-12 | Create short bullet audit (1 pager) and run 3 quick traces | solutions-engineering | 2 | customer: Acme Corp demo 2029-02-19
7 | quota-conflict | Reserved capacity overlapped with sandbox bursts | S2 | Jamal Singh | 2029-02-12 | Adjust autoscale policy to add buffer during scheduled sandboxes | dedicated | 3 | sandbox schedule: weekly Tue 09:00-11:00 UTC
8 | doc-gap | Missing runbook links for fallback policy in console | S3 | Aisha Rahman | 2029-02-12 | Draft runbook and attach to console route page | product-ops, console-and-rollouts | 4 | doc draft: /doc/runbooks/fallbacks/v1-draft

Quick filters to apply when using this as a sheet:
- Filter by Priority = S1 and sort Last seen desc to view urgent items.
- Filter Owner = "(blank)" to find unowned signals.

Owner responsibilities checklist:
- Triage within 2 business hours for S1, 1 business day for S2.
- Close rows with final note and date, then move to an archive sheet (monthly).
- If item requires follow-up beyond 6 weeks, create a persistent tracker in product or eng folder.

Notes / meta:
- This file intentionally minimal: no heavy attachments, just links.
- Expected lifespan is short; product-ops will sweep and delete archived rows monthly unless stakeholders ask to keep.
- If this sheet collects recurring items, we will convert to a lightweight dashboard in observability.

Recent changes log (freeform):
- 2029-02-11: Initial seed by Aisha; sample rows added from on-call notes.
- 2029-02-12: Marco added latency test row; Leah added embedding cost row.
- 2029-02-12: Minor formatting cleanup and checklist added.

Open questions:
- Do we need a "customer-visible" column for items that require customer comms? (ask: product comms)
- Should exports be automated to Slack channel #ops-lifecycle? (ask: eng-ops infra)

Next steps (short):
- Owners to fill in action items and update Last seen daily while active.
- Product-ops to review sheet once per weekday morning for escalations.

End of sheet.
